title: WHAT IF YOU COULD FEEL EVERYONE'S PAIN?

segments.line: Three months later, you're standing in a hospital emergency room.
Yeah. The one place you swore you'd never go.
But here's what the doctor figured out.
A lot of patients can't tell you where it hurts.
Babies.
People who don't speak English.
People who are too scared, or too confused, or just too tough to say anything.
You can't read their minds.
But you can see them. And when you see them... you know.
A toddler won't stop crying. Nobody can find anything wrong.
You look at him for two seconds... and your left ear is throbbing.
Ear infection.
An old man swears he's" fine, just tired."
Your chest goes tight.
The doctors run a test.
He's having a heart attack. They catch it in time.
By the end of the shift, you can barely stand.
You feel like you ran a marathon, broke your arm, and had three toothaches.
Because, kind of, you did.
But for the first time since this started, it doesn't feel like a curse.
It feels like a job. A job only you can do.
You walk out into the parking lot. The sun is coming up.
Your whole body hurts... and you're smiling.
You get home. Your roommate shuffles into the kitchen, half asleep...
and slams his toe into the table leg. Again.
Ouch. Your toe is on fire.
And for the first time since all this started... you laugh.
He looks at you like you're crazy.
You just grab two bags of frozen peas.
One for him. One for you.
Because maybe that's the whole point. When you feel everyone's pain... nobody has to hurt alone.
So, would you want this power? Or would it be too much? Tell me in the comments.
